title: AntiBP3: An improved method for predicting of antibacterial peptides using machine learning yechniques
abstract: Title:AntiBP3 Dataset – Experimentally validated antibacterial peptides (ABPs) against gram‑positive, gram‑negative, and gram‑variable bacteria Description: Project: AntiBP3 – A method for predicting antibacterial peptides against gram‑positive/negative/variable bacteria Publication: Bajiya, N., Choudhury, S., Dhall, A., & Raghava, G.P.S. (2024). AntiBP3: A Method for Predicting Antibacterial Peptides against Gram‑Positive/Negative/Variable Bacteria. Antibiotics, 13, 168. https://doi.org/10.3390/antibiotics13020168 Overview: This dataset accompanies AntiBP3, a method for predicting antibacterial peptides (ABPs) against three bacterial categories: gram‑positive (GP), gram‑negative (GN), and gram‑variable (GV). Unlike existing methods trained on limited or outdated data, AntiBP3 uses large, diverse datasets and develops separate group‑specific models. ABPs are short (8–50 aa), cationic, amphipathic peptides that kill bacteria via membrane disruption or intracellular mechanisms, offering an advantage over traditional antibiotics in reduced resistance development. Content: The dataset contains non‑redundant ABPs (APD3, AntiBP2, dbAMP 2.0, CAMPR3, DRAMP, ABP‑Finder) and non‑ABPs (randomly selected from Swiss‑Prot/UniProt, excluding ABPs). Category ABPs Non‑ABPs (training) Non‑ABPs (validation) Gram‑positive (GP) 930 744 + 744 186 + 186 Gram‑negative (GN) 1,455 1,164 + 1,164 291 + 291 Gram‑variable (GV) 8,985 7,188 + 7,188 1,797 + 1,797 Key Findings – Compositional analysis (ABPs enriched in): GP: Leu, Lys, Arg, Cys, Trp GN: Leu, Lys, Arg, Trp, Pro GV: Leu, Lys, Arg, Trp Positively charged Lys and Arg dominate; Gly and Leu (hydrophobic) aid membrane integration. Positional preferences (N‑terminus / C‑terminus): GP: Lys, Arg, Ala, Leu, Phe (N); Gly, Trp, Arg, Lys (C) GN: Lys, Val, Arg, Leu, Phe (N); Lys, Arg, Leu, Trp (C) GV: Gly, Phe, Lys, Arg, Ile, Leu (N); Lys, Leu, Arg, Trp, Phe, Ile, Gly (C) Exclusive motifs (MERCI, fp=10/20/30): GP: YGN, YGNG, YGNGV, NNG GN: RPPR, PRPR, RRIY, LPRP Best Model Performance (validation set – AAB NC‑terminal binary features): Category Model AUC MCC Accuracy Sensitivity Specificity GP RF 0.93 0.71 85.5% 80.7% 90.3% GN ET 0.98 0.87 93.6% 92.4% 94.9% GV SVC 0.94 0.74 87.0% 83.9% 90.1% Cross‑prediction analysis (trained on GP → tested on GN/GV): AUC dropped from 0.93 to 0.85/0.88 → confirms need for group‑specific models. Comparison with existing methods (validation set): Method GP AUC GN AUC GV AUC AntiBP3 0.93 0.98 0.94 AI4AMP 0.90 0.62 0.93 AMPScanner v2 0.79 0.54 0.80 iAMPpred 0.75 0.57 0.78 AMPfun 0.83 0.58 0.87 ABP‑Finder — — — Alignment‑based methods (BLAST, motif) had high precision but poor coverage; hybrid models (BLAST+ML, MOTIF+ML) did not outperform ML alone. Usage: Predicting antibacterial peptides for specific bacterial classes, designing novel ABPs, scanning protein sequences for antibacterial regions, assessing peptide‑based therapeutics against drug‑resistant strains.
